methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops delivered by a local Norfolk native directly enable grassroots capability building in a non-metro region, modeling the peer-to-peer knowledge distribution mechanism that could counter concentration trends.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's formal partnership with AI Ready RVA signals institutional commitment to deep capability development, but its metro-centered structure risks reinforcing Richmond as an excellence hub rather than distributing expertise across Virginia's rural regions.

signals.title: Children’s National and Virginia Tech deepen pediatric AI collaboration to accelerate innovation for children - Children's National Hospital
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's pediatric AI innovation hub concentrates advanced research capability in Blacksburg, deepening technical excellence in one location but creating questions about knowledge transfer pathways to clinicians and communities statewide.

signals.title: Tech Briefs: AI use strong in Virginia, with Montgomery County at No. 5 statewide - Cardinal News
signals.signal_reading: Montgomery County ranking #5 statewide in AI use suggests platform-delivered tools enable adoption even outside NoVA, but without detail on depth versus consumption, this likely reflects shallow ChatGPT-style usage rather than custom capability building.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: Explicit acknowledgment that AI data center infrastructure concentrates economic benefits in already-advantaged NoVA corridors while imposing infrastructure costs elsewhere crystallizes the urban-rural divide that defines the Widening Gap scenario.
